- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model frequently overestimates near-term decline — apply 10–15% downward adjustment to early forecast days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast shows persistent downward trend despite sentiment suggesting stability, add 0.5–1.0 point upward bias in middle-to-late period.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility — increase forecast variance by 10–20% in final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
